clue.text: Sonata form of flit?

definitions.meaning: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 14 is popularly known by this nickname
a ... flit is a secret night-time move to dodge the rent

explanation.surface: A musical query: is a sonata some kind of flitting?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sonata form' is a real musical term, which tempts you to read it as one phrase; the split falls after 'Sonata'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's famous sonata carries this nickname, and the word also prefixes 'flit' in the idiom for a furtive escape.

clue.text: Wet one's in majority

indicators.note: 'in' says the one goes inside the word for the majority

parts.note: most means the greater part, the majority
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A damp individual belongs to the larger group.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist describes something slightly wet or damp.

clue.text: Rhetoric of a socialist or otherwise …

parts.note: taken as written
the alternative to a socialist in British politics is a Tory, a Conservative

explanation.surface: A remark on the speech-making of a left-winger, or perhaps of someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A socialist or otherwise' expands to 'a socialist or a Tory', and the last three words give the answer; 'socialist' only sets up the contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of public speaking, the skilled use of rhetoric.

clue.text: … brought up in socialism, which is unprofessional

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
'in' says the letters sit inside the word socialism

explanation.surface: Following on from the last clue, a claim that socialism is amateurish.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to 2 down's socialist; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means lay, belonging to the laity rather than the clergy or a profession.

clue.text: Criminal band go from Glasgow

definitions.meaning: a band of criminals is a mob of crooks
in Scots dialect, spoken in Glasgow

explanation.surface: Crooks are told to clear out of a Scottish city.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a group of crooks, and in Scots the same word is the verb to go.

clue.text: It's very big, but with treatment sure to mend

indicators.note: letters that get treatment are worked over and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient is told the problem is huge but treatment will cure it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous means huge or enormous in size or degree.

clue.text: Discrimination starts showing in the gallery

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the first letter of showing goes inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

indicators.note: the start of the word showing is its opening letter only

explanation.surface: Signs of discernment begin to show at an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrimination in the sense of fine judgement in aesthetic matters is good taste.

clue.text: Paper's consumer publication said when to …

parts.note: The Times is a British national newspaper

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so the magazine title is heard as a word of the same sound

parts.note: Which? is the British consumer magazine that tests products

explanation.surface: A newspaper's consumer magazine announced the timing of something to be continued.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on into 7 down: the device tells you when to stop, or switch on and off. Which? is the British consumer-testing magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock-controlled switch decides when a heater or light is to come on or go off.

clue.text: … stop and shout awfully loudly

indicators.note: done awfully means badly, so the letters of shout are mangled

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Continuing from 6 down, someone is told to quit and yells horribly at full volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut off a supply or machine is to stop it.

clue.text: Short-lived help — a mere tinkering

indicators.note: tinkering means fiddling about with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A little fiddling gives help that does not last long.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral means lasting only a short time, like a mayfly.

clue.text: It could be Gordon's partner

parts.note: Gordon's is a brand of gin, and in the drink 'gin and It' the It is short for a sweet Italian fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone wonders who might be paired with a man named Gordon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gordon' looks like a person, and the setter's own pseudonym Gordius adds to the tease; Gordon's is the gin brand, and 'It' in 'gin and It' is the abbreviation the clue begins with.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic British cocktail gin and It mixes gin, such as Gordon's, with a sweet red vermouth from Italy.

clue.text: Play about with a gun?

indicators.note: 'about' here means turned round, so the play's title is read backwards

parts.note: Loot is a comic play by Joe Orton

explanation.surface: Someone fools around while carrying a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play about' reads as one phrase meaning mess around; 'about' is really the reversal signal applied to an Orton title.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a handgun is called by this word, as in being 'tooled up' for a job.

clue.text: Where the Sun gets going more snow is unlikely

indicators.note: something unlikely is out of the ordinary, so these letters are put into an unexpected arrangement

explanation.surface: A weather forecast says the sun will come out and further snow is improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a forecast; the Sun is in fact the British tabloid newspaper, and the definition names the room where its stories are set in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's editorial office, where reports are gathered and pages prepared, is called this.

clue.text: Basic facts of loads beneath supporters?

indicators.note: in a down answer, beneath puts the loads below the supporters

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments
stacks means loads, a large quantity

explanation.surface: Fundamental truths about a heap set below some braces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests fans or bracing beams; it is the lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to brass tacks means dealing with the essential, fundamental facts of a matter.

clue.text: Case copper makes for non-combatant organisation

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder are made into a new word, so the phrase signals rearrangement

explanation.surface: A police officer's investigation goes to a pacifist body.
explanation.definitionFit: The American Peace Corps sends civilian volunteers abroad for development work, not military service.

clue.text: Swain keeps fiery type in restraint

indicators.note: a bond that keeps something holds it inside, so the reworked letters sit within it

parts.note: a bond is a tie or fetter that restrains

indicators.note: a type is a variety or version, taken here as a recasting of the letters of fiery

explanation.surface: A suitor holds back his hot-tempered nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiery type' looks like a description of a person; 'type' is the setter's rather loose anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Swain is an old poetic word for a young lover or suitor, the man a woman is going out with.

clue.text: Lawyers' den can be arranged for a social occasion

parts.note: the Bar is the collective term for barristers

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Barristers' chambers can be set up for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn dance is a social gathering with country dancing, originally held in a barn.

clue.text: Conclude that hell is a no-no?

indicators.note: a no-no is something not allowed, so the word no is barred from the synonym for hell

parts.note: the inferno is hell, as in Dante

explanation.surface: Someone decides that damnation is forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence.

clue.text: Breeds found at Ascot

definitions.meaning: breeds and ... are both groups of animals or peoples sharing descent
Ascot is an English racecourse famous for Royal Ascot, where horse competitions are held

explanation.surface: Particular lines of horse are to be seen at the Royal meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a breed or stock, and contests of speed are what Ascot racecourse stages.

clue.text: Whig can get involved in conversation

indicators.note: letters that get involved are tangled together and come out reordered

explanation.surface: A Whig politician is drawn into a discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinwag is informal British slang for a chat or gossip.

clue.text: Former PM finds urchin shivering with cold

annotationWithheld.why: Former PM finds urchin shivering with cold (9): the parse splits 'urchin' into URCH plus 'in', so the one word is both fodder and the insertion indicator putting URCH into CHILL
annotationWithheld.clue: Former PM finds urchin shivering with cold

clue.text: Make investigation in papers

parts.note: taken as written
a quire is a set of twenty-four or twenty-five sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Someone researches something in documents.
explanation.definitionFit: To inquire is to ask questions or investigate.

clue.text: It floats aimlessly, if direct

indicators.note: moving aimlessly means wandering in no fixed order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something drifts about without purpose, the opposite of going straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose fragments of sea ice carried by wind and current are a floating mass.

clue.text: Somewhat less than 2 pints water

indicators.note: somewhat less than the whole means a little is cut off the end of the measure

parts.note: a quart is a measure of two pints

explanation.surface: A drink measure falls just short of a quart of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is the Latin word for water, used in English in names and labels.

clue.text: Abolish yearly with a disappearance

indicators.note: the disappearance of the a means that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: annual means happening every year

explanation.surface: Someone scraps a yearly event that has vanished.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to cancel or declare void, such as a marriage or a law.

clue.text: Pigeon plunged in Texas

definitions.meaning: a bird of the pigeon family
in American English the past tense of dive is ...

explanation.surface: A bird dived into the water in the Lone Star State.
explanation.walkthrough: Texas stands for American usage generally, where dove replaces British dived.
explanation.definitionFit: Doves and pigeons belong to the same bird family, and dove is the American past of dive.

clue.text: Apartment in which one's settled

indicators.note: 'in which' says the one sits within the apartment

parts.note: pad is slang for a flat or home
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A flat where someone has made their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' tempts as a description of moving into the flat; it means a bill has been paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled bill or debt is one that has been paid off.

clue.text: In snow poor react badly to publisher employing hacks

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Bad weather leaves people responding poorly to a publisher's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacks' suggests journalists, and also the phone hacking scandal that engulfed this Murdoch company's British papers in 2011.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Murdoch's media group published newspapers staffed by journalists, informally called hacks.

clue.text: East End garden boundaries?

parts.note: a Cockney from London's East End drops the h sound, so the leafy borders round a garden are said without their first letter

explanation.surface: A question about where gardens in east London end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' first reads as the eastern end of a garden; it is London's East End, whose Cockney accent drops an initial h from the word for leafy garden borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Edges are borders or boundaries, and hedges are what mark the boundaries of a garden.

clue.text: Spooner's curse on unwanted growth of a flower?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of word pairs, so the two synonyms exchange initial consonants

parts.note: a weed is a plant growing where it is not wanted
a spell can be a curse cast on someone

explanation.surface: A gardener puts a curse on an unwanted plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica, a small plant with blue blooms, is commonly known by this name.
